Create a Character Sheet in ChatGPT Image 2.0 (full visual description + front view, side profile, close-up) and reuse it as the consistency anchor for every Seedance shot  
Write a scene-by-scene storyboard prompt in ChatGPT that specifies concept, tone, number of shots, timing, plus shot type, camera movement, and action for each frame before generating any video  
Generate each storyboard frame as a separate image (one prompt per shot) and upload the Character Sheet as a reference every time to lock character consistency across frames  
In Dreamina, use Seedance 2.0 Image-to-Video by uploading each storyboard frame as the first frame so the model inherits composition, lighting, and character positioning  
Enable JSON mode in Dreamina (Normal/JSON toggle) and use the JSON prompt field to set motion intensity, camera movement, and shot duration per clip for directed scenes  
Set Seedance clip duration to ~5 seconds for regular scenes and 8–10 seconds for transformation sequences  
Run a first Seedance generation as a test, then adjust the JSON prompt before doing final generations  
In editing, trim the first and last 0.5 seconds of each generated clip to tighten pacing  
Choose Cross Dissolve for smooth transitions and Hard Cut for sharp cuts when assembling clips in sequence  
Sync transformation moments to the music beat during the edit rather than relying on generation timing alone

- Entiende el contexto de la conversación — recuerda imágenes y personajes anteriores
